Connection is infrastructure — treat recurring in-person social contact as a health input
Forensics should feed prevention, not blame — for chronic multifactorial disease the highest-probability causes are the still-controllable ones
Gut microbiome resilience is an output of diet/behavior, not an input you can dose
Measure the trend, not the snapshot — and don't over-test into anxiety
Match the intervention to the individual, not to the trend
Convergence beats accumulation — rank interventions by how many goals each serves
Long exhale = calm, fast inhale = alert — the breath is a free, portable nervous-system switch
Deodorant masks odor, antiperspirant (aluminum) stops sweat — and the aluminum-cancer/Alzheimer's fears don't survive the absorbed dose
The drink is not the supplement — default to the food/beverage form, treat concentrated extracts as drugs
Date-check every dated claim from web search — aggregator summaries recycle stale content as current
~7,000 steps/day captures most of the benefit — the 10,000 goal is 1960s marketing, not science
Bad posture" is not a reliable cause of back/neck pain — movement variety is the real lever
For sleep, regularity beats duration — a consistent wake time is a bigger lever than total hours
Eat with the seasons" is a good habit on a weak literal claim — the real levers are freshness, plant variety, cost, and taste
Clean eating and cheap eating are the same grocery list — and spoilage, not price, is the hidden cost
Health testing — cadence beats coverage; keep two clocks and separate the menu from the calendar
Treats inflammation" ≠ "manages the stress response" — and mechanism-plausible ≠ proven
Evaluate any herbal/traditional remedy on TWO axes — does it work, AND is it safe for me
When a risky remedy proves a body target is reachable, find the FOOD that reaches it — not the concentrated pill
The calm-body → less-inflammation link runs through a real named nerve circuit — so the free habits are genuine therapy, not optional wellness

Gut-directed hypnotherapy is a real, guideline-recognized non-drug therapy for the gut-brain axis — and the only one of its class with colitis-remission evidence — but strictly an add-on whose payoff depends on finishing the course
For acute stress, body-based tools calm you faster than thinking your way calm — do the breath first, then layer a reframe; two popular tricks are commonly mis-stated
A policy/tariff/regulatory thesis named after a proclamation's headline category is not self-verifying — check the specific instrument against the actual legal text, not the theme
Migraine is partly a clock-timed disorder — a fixed wake time is a mechanism-matched, dual-system lever

When a thesis rests on a legal/regulatory mechanism, write an explicit "thesis-break" leg into the exit conditions at filing time — so a broken thesis can trigger a mechanical close the same run it's found, instead of waiting on a discretionary call plus a fresh quote
Cold sores can only be suppressed, not cured (best non-drug lever is stress + lip SPF); allergy "reversal" is desensitization, not a cure — and food OIT raises anaphylaxis risk

PEA (palmitoylethanolamide) is the first nutraceutical candidate for the stress→mast-cell→gut-barrier pathway that doesn't collide with the CYP enzymes autoimmune meds rely on — but evidence is IBS not UC, so it's a provider conversation, never a self-start

Helminth ("worm") therapy for inflammatory bowel disease is not evidence-based — the promising 2005 pilot did not replicate, and the definitive modern RCTs are negative; the valid residue of the "Old Friends"/hygiene-mismatch idea is a diverse plant/fiber/fermented diet and early-life microbial exposure, not a treatment for established disease

The strongest evidence-based ways to support an easier labor & delivery are behavioral/positional, not supplements — continuous one-to-one labor support (biggest effect from a doula), upright/mobile first-stage positions, and prenatal exercise lead; several popular "natural induction" supplements do not hold up

Inflammatory bowel disease modestly raises cardiovascular risk, but the excess is activity-dependent — it concentrates in flares/active disease and normalizes to the general population during remission, so staying in remission is itself cardiovascular prevention
